missing_links.mechanism: LCS as last-passage percolation on a lattice with Bernoulli(1/2) weights is equivalent to a maximum-weight monotone partial coupling -- precisely an optimal transport problem with order constraints. The Kantorovich dual of this OT problem yields a variational formula: gamma_2 = inf_{phi} E[sum_j max_i {1_{a_i=b_j} - phi(i,j)}]. The Busemann functions from LPP theory are exactly the optimal dual potentials in the OT formulation, connecting the Cator-Pimentel competition interface to Kantorovich duality.
missing_links.rationale: This link unifies two currently separate bounding strategies. The LPP shape function approach and the OT relaxation approach both yield upper bounds on gamma_2, but through different relaxations. Recognizing their shared dual structure (Busemann functions = Kantorovich potentials) means: (1) LPP geodesic techniques can construct better OT dual solutions, potentially tightening the upper bound below Lueker's 0.826280; (2) the Sinkhorn algorithm with monotonicity constraints provides a computational path to approximate Busemann functions; (3) the competition interface from LPP gives geometric insight into which monotonicity constraints are tight in the OT relaxation.

The hierarchy gamma_BM < gamma(W_1) < gamma(W_2) < ... < gamma_2 constitutes a systematic cavity expansion where each periodic word captures correlations at a specific range, and the mean-field value is the k=1 (i.i.d.) limit.

This yields: (1) a monotone sequence of lower bounds gamma(W_k) converging to gamma_2, (2) a quantitative measure of the correlation gap as a function of correlation range, and (3) a prediction for the rate at which periodic-word bounds approach gamma_2, informing how large k must be to beat the current best lower bound of 0.792666.

analysis_summary: The concept tree has 12 nodes and 17 directed edges. Analysis reveals structural imbalance: the statistical-mechanics chain (001->003->004->009->011) and the optimization chain (005->008->011) are well-connected internally but poorly cross-linked to each other and to theoretical foundations (010, 012). Five high-value missing links were identified: (1) subadditive_ergodic -> kpz_universality bridges convergence rate theory with scaling exponents; (2) cellular_automata -> kpz_universality connects transfer matrices with KPZ scaling functions; (3) optimal_transport -> last_passage_percolation unifies Kantorovich duality with Busemann functions for tighter upper bounds; (4) mean_field_cavity -> frog_dynamics reveals periodic-word bounds as systematic cavity corrections to mean-field; (5) cellular_automata -> subadditive_ergodic provides a second subadditive axis (width L) independent of string length n. Links 1-3 have high bound-improvement potential because they create new computational or theoretical pathways to tighten the current best bounds [0.792666, 0.826280] on gamma_2.
